definition: means a cost-sharing requirement under a health insurance policy that provides that the insurer will not be liable for a specified rupee amount in case of indemnity policies and for a specified number of days / hours in case of hospital cash policies which will apply before any benefits are payable by the insurer. A deductible does not reduce the Sum Insured. The deductible is separate from any Aggregate Deductible that may be in-force and applicable under the Policy, as specified in the Policy Schedule.
plain: An amount you cover yourself before the policy starts paying at all. Below it, the insurer pays nothing; above it, they pay the rest.
whyItMatters: This is the mechanism behind super top-up plans: you accept a high deductible — say ₹5 lakh — in exchange for a much cheaper premium on a large cover, and you rely on a base policy or your savings to bridge the gap underneath. It only works if that bridge actually exists. A deductible with nothing under it is just an uninsured first ₹5 lakh.
